title: Granular feature runway oscillation and pricing impulse matrix
content:
Purpose:
Quick experiment-style sheet to show how feature-level demand swings + a sudden pricing impulse (±20% effective token price) propagate through burn, runway, and hiring gates. Designed to feed SRE/ProdOps and Product prioritization conversations.

Status/notes: draft — use for week-of-2026-12-06 triage. Not yet validated with full Monte Carlo; small-sample sims run locally (see MR above).

High-level assumptions (baseline):
- Base headcount cost per FTE (loaded): $22k/month (avg across engineering/product/infra mix for feature teams).
- Baseline non-payroll opex (GPU, infra, cloud): $1.1M/mo across org at current load.
- Token mix baseline: 65% generation, 30% embeddings, 5% rerank; average price per effective token unit = $0.006 in baseline.
- Product-led growth sensitivity window: demand elasticity approximated as linear within ±30% price movement (early estimate).
- Hiring lag: 8 weeks from req to productive ramp (conservative).
- Safety cushion: maintain >= 4 weeks of cash runway for payroll-only.

Summary table (monthly snapshot style) — columns are comma-separated for quick paste:
Month, Net New Feature FTEs (hires), Cumulative FTE, Payroll Burn ($k), Infra Burn ($k), Total Burn ($k), Effective token price multiplier, Demand delta vs baseline (%), Monthly revenue proxy ($k), Runway months (at current cash buffer 12,000k)
2026-12, 4, 156, 3432, 1100, 4532, 1.00, 0, 2200, 2.65
2027-01, 6, 162, 3564, 1180, 4744, 0.80, +12, 2464, 2.52
2027-02, 2, 164, 3608, 1250, 4858, 0.80, +10, 2520, 2.47
2027-03, 0, 164, 3608, 1275, 4883, 1.20, -18, 2064, 2.91
2027-04, 0, 164, 3608, 1260, 4868, 1.20, -15, 2120, 2.92

Interpretation: under a sudden price cut (0.8x) we see demand +10–12% in early months (short-run elasticity), which increases revenue proxy and slightly improves runway. A price increase (1.2x) produces sharp demand drop (~15–18%) that hurts revenue and therefore effective runway even though per-token revenue is higher — because demand loss compounds fixed payroll + infra.

Feature-level impulse matrix (how to think about prioritization):
- Rows: feature buckets (core-routing, embeddings-enhancements, developer-UX, monitoring/observability).
- Columns: three shock types (price-cut +20% adoption uplift, price-increase +15% adoption loss, capacity-constrained infra +25% infra cost).
- Cell = expected net-monthly margin delta ($k) + recommended hiring action (accelerate/maintain-freeze).

Example cells (sketch):
core-routing: price-cut => +420k margin delta, action: accelerate 2 hires; price-up => -360k, action: hiring freeze + reassign 1 contractor; infra-cost-shock => -180k, action: defer non-essential infra projects
embeddings-enhancements: price-cut => +220k, action: accelerate 1 hire; price-up => -120k, action: maintain; infra-cost-shock => -90k, action: partial runbook optimization
dev-ux: price-cut => +110k, action: maintain; price-up => -40k, action: defer new UI experiments; infra-cost-shock => -10k, action: no immediate change
monitoring/observability: price-cut => +30k, action: maintain; price-up => -20k, action: reduce external vendor spend

Hiring gate rules (proposal for playbook):
- Green (go): projected net margin delta across next 3 months > cost of hire (3 months loaded) + 10% buffer AND runway impact <= -0.25 months.
- Yellow (caution): margin delta between 0 and cost-of-hire -> require exec signoff + 30d pilot (contract-first).
- Red (hold): margin delta < 0 (i.e., expected to worsen burn) OR runway would shorten by >0.5 months.
- Auto-freeze trigger: if cash runway <= 2.5 months OR Monte Carlo 90% CI lower bound < 1.5 months.

Sensitivity slice: pricing impulse vs headcount acceleration
- Scenario A: cut price by 20% and accelerate hiring by 8 FTEs across core-routing and embeddings in 2 months -> short-term revenue +8%, burn +6%, runway net +0.1 months.
- Scenario B: raise price by 20%, freeze hires -> revenue -17%, burn -3.5%, runway -0.7 months (worse).
- Key takeaway: for Redwood-style offering with high fixed payroll, small price increases can reduce overall margin if elasticity strong; conversely, targeted cuts coupled with aggressive feature hires can expand demand enough to offset hiring cost (but dependent on feature ROI).

Small-sample Monte Carlo notes (quick):
- Ran 2k samples varying elasticity (normal mu=0.12 sd=0.06 clipped [0,0.4]), hiring ramp (mu=8w sd=2w), infra cost shock (mu=0 sd=0.12).
- 90% CI for runway under Scenario B (price-up) shortened by 0.4–1.1 months (bad tail exists).
- Action: increase buffer to 5 weeks if leadership favors price increases as default.

Open questions / to validate:
- Elasticity by customer segment (startup versus enterprise) — need route-level token mix and cohort elasticities (product/analytics to deliver).
- True effective per-token revenue after discounts/rebates — downstream billing credits not modeled.
- Correlation between infra-cost shocks and demand (e.g., if infra degrades, demand falls faster).
- Impact of Dedicated & Private customers (committed revenue should be modeled separately in next iteration).

Immediate next steps (owner: Asha / finance ops):
1) Hook up latest usage exports (prod-usage route-level) to the MR sim and re-run 10k-sample Monte Carlo with segmented elasticity assumptions (due 2026-12-10).
2) Work with Product (Liam) to provide per-feature revenue attribution for last 6 months (due 2026-12-08).
3) Draft a one-page hiring-gate checklist for PGMs and Finance signoff (Marisol, due 2026-12-07).
4) Run sensitivity with committed revenue stripped out (on-prem/VPC) and surface to Sales Ops (Evan) — 2026-12-14.
